definition_en: an angry disagreement, or a set of reasons offered for or against an idea
core_image: 两张纸上的理由被并排摆着对照
scene: 两人从厨房吵到客厅。Their argument lasted until midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 argument 是「争吵」（第 1 个义项：激烈的口头冲突）；句意是他们的争吵一直持续到午夜。

senses.title: An angry disagreement
senses.definition: a heated exchange between people who disagree
senses.definitionCN: 意见不合的人之间激烈的言语往来
senses.example: Their argument lasted until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的争吵一直持续到午夜。
senses.why: Latin argumentum meant a proof; two people each pressing proofs at each other turn the exchange into a quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 argumentum 意为「证明」；两人各拿一套证明互相压过去，这场交流就变成了争吵。

senses.title: A reason offered in support
senses.definition: a statement and its supporting reasons put forward in a discussion
senses.definitionCN: 讨论中提出的主张连同支持它的理由
senses.example: The main argument for the plan is that it saves time.
senses.exampleCN: 支持这项计划的主要论据是它能节省时间。
senses.why: This is the word's older and more technical sense: an argument is a case built to make a conclusion clear.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词更早也更专业的义项：argument 是为了让结论变清楚而搭起来的一整套理由。

intro.en: Argument is the noun of the Latin verb for making a matter clear.
intro.cn: argument 是拉丁语中表示「使事情清楚」的动词所对应的名词。

items.en: arguere meant 'to make clear, to prove'.
items.cn: arguere 意为「使清楚、证明」。

items.en: argumentum meant 'a proof, a clarifying statement'.
items.cn: argumentum 意为「证明、使事情清楚的说法」。

items.en: French kept the sense of a reasoned case.
items.cn: 法语保留了「有推理的说法」这一义。

items.en: English used it for both proof and dispute.
items.cn: 英语兼用其「论证」与「争执」两义。

items.en: Everyday speech favours the quarrel sense, academic writing the proof sense.
items.cn: 日常口语偏重争吵义，学术写作偏重论证义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the argue stem; the near-meaning group splits dispute from reasoning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 argue 词干；近义组把争执类与说理类分开。

entries.definition: the process of thinking things through

normalIntro.en: An argument is either a clash or a case.
normalIntro.cn: argument 要么是一场冲突，要么是一套理由。

normal.en: Have an argument means to quarrel.
normal.cn: have an argument 意为吵了一架。

normal.en: An argument for or against names the side.
normal.cn: argument for 或 against 点明立场。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the e out of the noun.
normal.cn: 名词拼写中没有那个 e。

normal.en: It can also mean a line of reasoning in a paper.
normal.cn: 它也可指论文中的一条论证线索。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-gu-ment.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-gu-ment。

abstract.en: See two lists of reasons laid side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象两张理由清单并排摆着。

abstract.en: See a raised finger counting a point.
abstract.cn: 想象竖起手指数一条论点。

abstract.en: See a door slammed mid-sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象话没说完门就被摔上。

examples.en: Their argument lasted until midnight.
examples.cn: 他们的争吵一直持续到午夜。

examples.en: The main argument for the plan is that it saves time.
examples.cn: 支持这项计划的主要论据是它能节省时间。

examples.en: She won the argument with a single fact.
examples.cn: 她用一个事实就在争论中占了上风。

dict_mnemonic.text: argue（论证）加 -ment：把理由摆出来，摆得拢是论证，摆不拢就是争吵。

root: 来自拉丁语 argumentum「证明」，源自动词 arguere「使清楚、证明」；由「说清道理」分化出论据与争吵两义。

sensesIntro.en: One noun holds both the calm case and the loud quarrel it can become.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词既装着冷静的理由，也装着它可能演变成的争吵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sets of reasons pushed toward each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两套理由互相推挤。

intro.en: A Latin noun of proof that English uses for quarrels too.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示证明的拉丁名词，英语也用它指争吵。

latinIntro.en: The verb arguere, 'to make clear', is the base of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 动词 arguere「使清楚」是整个词族的根基。

definition_en: the branch of mathematics that deals with numbers and their basic operations
core_image: 黑板上排着加减乘除的竖式
scene: 老师没有用计算器，只让他们在心里算。Mental arithmetic is part of the test.
sceneCN: 这里 arithmetic 是「算术」（第 1 个义项：研究数与基本运算的学科）；句意是心算也是考试的一部分。

senses.title: The study of numbers
senses.definition: the school subject that teaches adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing
senses.definitionCN: 教授加减乘除的学科
senses.example: Mental arithmetic is part of the test.
senses.exampleCN: 心算也是考试的一部分。
senses.why: Greek arithmos meant 'number' and tekhnē meant 'art', so arithmetike was literally the art of numbers.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arithmos 意为「数」，tekhnē 意为「技艺」，所以 arithmetike 字面上就是「数的技艺」。

senses.title: The act of calculating
senses.definition: the working out of sums with numbers
senses.definitionCN: 用数字把结果算出来的过程
senses.example: The arithmetic behind the budget is simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这份预算背后的计算很简单。
senses.why: The name of the subject extends to the activity itself: what one does in arithmetic is arithmetic.
senses.whyCN: 学科的名称扩展到活动本身：在算术里所做的运算，也叫 arithmetic。

intro.en: Arithmetic is a Greek compound meaning 'the art of number'.
intro.cn: arithmetic 是希腊语复合词，意为「数的技艺」。

items.en: arithmos meant 'number, count'.
items.cn: arithmos 意为「数、计数」。

items.en: tekhnē meant 'art, skill'.
items.cn: tekhnē 意为「技艺、技能」。

items.en: arithmetike tekhnē was the skill of counting.
items.cn: arithmetike tekhnē 即计数的技艺。

items.en: Latin kept the word as the name of a school subject.
items.cn: 拉丁语把它保留为一门学校科目之名。

items.en: English arithmetic named one of the seven liberal arts.
items.cn: 英语 arithmetic 曾是七艺之一。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group gives broader or narrower number words.
note.cn: 形近组同出一个希腊词干；近义组是范围更大或更窄的数的词。

entries.definition: the wider study of number and shape
the working out of a result

normalIntro.en: Arithmetic is the craft of number.
normalIntro.cn: arithmetic 就是关于数的技艺。

normal.en: The th is pronounced as in thick.
normal.cn: 其中的 th 读作 thick 里的音。

normal.en: Mental arithmetic means sums done in the head.
normal.cn: mental arithmetic 指心算。

normal.en: The adjective is arithmetical.
normal.cn: 形容词是 arithmetical。

normal.en: It names a branch, not a single sum.
normal.cn: 它指一门分支，而非某一道算式。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-RITH-me-tic.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-RITH-me-tic。

abstract.en: See columns of figures on a blackboard.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上成列的数字。

abstract.en: See fingers counting under a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象桌下掰着的手指。

abstract.en: See a plus sign drawn in chalk.
abstract.cn: 想象粉笔画的加号。

examples.en: Mental arithmetic is part of the test.
examples.cn: 心算也是考试的一部分。

examples.en: The arithmetic behind the budget is simple.
examples.cn: 这份预算背后的计算很简单。

examples.en: Children learn arithmetic before algebra.
examples.cn: 孩子们先学算术，再学代数。

dict_mnemonic.text: arithm（数）加 -etic（技艺）：与数打交道的技艺，就是算术。

root: 源自希腊语 arithmetike tekhnē「计数的技艺」，由 arithmos「数」与 tekhnē「技艺」构成，经拉丁语 arithmetica 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The art of number names both a school subject and the summing done inside it.
sensesIntro.cn: 数的技艺既指一门课程，也指课程里所做的运算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of figures waiting to be added.
core.cn: 核心意象：一列等着相加的数字。

intro.en: A Greek compound that became the name of a school subject.
intro.cn: 这个希腊语复合词后来成了一门课程的名称。

latinIntro.en: The number root arithmos also appears in logarithm.
latinIntro.cn: 数词根 arithmos 也出现在 logarithm 中。

definition_zh: 手臂；武器；武装；分支机构
definition_en: the upper limb of the body, a weapon, the act of supplying weapons, or a branch of an organisation
core_image: 一条伸出去的手臂，握紧时也能当武器
scene: 他从梯子上下来，胳膊擦破了皮。She broke her arm skiing last winter.
sceneCN: 这里 arm 是「手臂」（第 1 个义项：身体的上肢）；句意是她去年冬天滑雪时摔断了胳膊。

pos.zh: 名词：手臂；武器；分支机构

senses.title: The upper limb
senses.definition: the part of the body from shoulder to hand
senses.definitionCN: 从肩到手之间的身体部位
senses.example: She broke her arm skiing last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年冬天滑雪时摔断了胳膊。
senses.why: Latin armus meant 'shoulder', and the joint that hangs from it gave English the limb word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 armus 意为「肩」，挂在肩上的这个关节部位就给了英语「手臂」这个词。

senses.title: A weapon
senses.definition: an instrument made for fighting, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 为作战而制造的器械，通常用复数
senses.example: The treaty limits the sale of small arms.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约限制小型武器的销售。
senses.why: A separate Latin word arma meant 'tools of war'; the two words merged in form but kept separate meanings.
senses.whyCN: 另一个拉丁词 arma 意为「战具」；两个词形式合并，意义却各自保留。

senses.title: To supply with weapons
senses.definition: to give someone weapons or equipment
senses.definitionCN: 把武器或装备交给某人
senses.example: The rebels armed themselves with stolen rifles.
senses.exampleCN: 叛乱者用偷来的步枪武装自己。
senses.why: From the noun for weapons came the verb: to arm a group is to put arms into its hands.
senses.whyCN: 由「武器」这一名词生出动词：arm 一群人就是把武器交到他们手上。

senses.title: A branch of an organisation
senses.definition: one part of a larger body that reaches out like a limb
senses.definitionCN: 大机构中像肢体一样伸出去的一个部分
senses.example: The research arm of the company hires many scientists.
senses.exampleCN: 公司的研究部门雇了许多科学家。
senses.why: The limb image works for institutions: a branch reaches out from the main body as an arm does.
senses.whyCN: 肢体的形象适用于机构：分支像手臂一样从主体伸出去。

intro.en: English arm joins two Latin words that looked alike: one for the shoulder, one for weapons.
intro.cn: 英语 arm 合并了两个形似的拉丁词：一个指肩，一个指武器。

items.en: armus meant 'shoulder, upper arm'.
items.cn: armus 意为「肩、上臂」。

items.en: earm was the native word for the limb.
items.cn: earm 是表示肢体的本族词。

items.en: arma meant 'weapons, tools of war'.
items.cn: arma 意为「武器、战具」。

items.en: French armes brought the weapon sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 armes 把「武器」义带入英语。

items.en: The two senses share one spelling, and the branch sense grew from the limb.
items.cn: 两种意义共用一个拼写，分支义则由肢体义发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same short stem; the near-meaning group gives the limb, the weapon, and the branch.
note.cn: 形近组共享这一短词干；近义组分别给肢体、武器与分支。

normalIntro.en: One arm holds, the other arms.
normalIntro.cn: 一条手臂用来拿东西，另一条用来拿起武器。

normal.en: The body part is countable: one arm, two arms.
normal.cn: 身体部位可数：一条手臂，两条手臂。

normal.en: Weapons usually appear in the plural arms.
normal.cn: 武器义通常用复数 arms。

normal.en: The verb arm takes a person or group as object.
normal.cn: 动词 arm 的宾语是人或群体。

normal.en: Arm in arm means side by side.
normal.cn: arm in arm 意为挽着手臂并肩而行。

normal.en: The word is short and flat: ARM.
normal.cn: 这个词短而平：ARM。

abstract.en: See a sleeve pushed up past the elbow.
abstract.cn: 想象袖子卷到肘部以上。

abstract.en: See a rifle leaning against a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一支步枪靠在墙边。

abstract.en: See a branch growing from a trunk.
abstract.cn: 想象一根枝条从树干伸出。

examples.en: She broke her arm skiing last winter.
examples.cn: 她去年冬天滑雪时摔断了胳膊。

examples.en: The treaty limits the sale of small arms.
examples.cn: 该条约限制小型武器的销售。

examples.en: The research arm of the company hires many scientists.
examples.cn: 公司的研究部门雇了许多科学家。

dict_mnemonic.text: arm 既可指手臂，也可指武器：手臂握紧器械，就成了武装。

root: 一词合两源：肢体义来自拉丁语 armus「肩」与古英语 earm；武器义来自拉丁语 arma「战具」，经法语 armes 进入英语；分支义由肢体比喻而来。

sensesIntro.en: A limb, the weapons it can hold, the act of handing them out, and any branch that reaches from a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条肢体、它握得住的武器、分发武器的动作，以及任何从主体伸出的分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an outstretched arm that can close into a fist.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条伸出去、又能握成拳的手臂。

intro.en: A short native word that absorbed a Latin word of war.
intro.cn: 这是一个短暂的本族词，吸收了一个拉丁语的战争词。

latinIntro.en: The weapon root arma also gives armour and army.
latinIntro.cn: 武器词根 arma 也派生出 armour 与 army。

items.meaning: as much as one arm holds

definition_en: a comfortable chair with supports for your arms
core_image: 一把带两个扶手的宽大椅子，坐下去像被手臂抱住
scene: 他在壁炉边坐下，翻开了那本旧书。He settled into his armchair by the fire and opened the old book.
sceneCN: 这里 armchair 是「扶手椅」（第 1 个义项：带扶手的单人座椅）；句意是他在壁炉边的扶手椅上坐下，翻开旧书。

pos.zh: 名词：扶手椅；单人沙发椅
形容词：只停留在口头上的，书斋式的（如 armchair critic）

collocations.zh: 只靠阅读图片旅行的「沙发旅行家」

derivatives.zh: armchair 的基础词，义为「椅子」
armchair 的构词成分，义为「手臂」，此处指椅子两侧的扶手
相关上位词，义为「座位；座椅（总称）」

senses.title: A chair with arm supports
senses.definition: a comfortable chair for one person, with parts on each side to rest the arms on
senses.definitionCN: 供单人乘坐的舒适座椅，两侧有可搁手臂的部件
senses.example: Grandfather reads the newspaper in his armchair every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父每天早上都坐在扶手椅里看报纸。
senses.why: The compound is literal: arm plus chair names the chair by its two armrests.
senses.whyCN: 复合词取字面义：arm（手臂）加 chair（椅子），用两侧扶手来命名这种椅子。

senses.title: Involving no real experience
senses.definition: based on reading or imagining rather than real practical experience
senses.definitionCN: 只靠阅读或想象，而非亲身实践得来的
senses.example: He is an armchair critic who has never run a business himself.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个没亲手经营过企业的空谈批评家。
senses.why: The image of the armchair is the seat of comfort and watching, so the word extends to anyone observing life from that seat instead of acting.
senses.whyCN: 扶手椅的画面是安逸旁观之位，由此引申指坐在椅上袖手旁观、不肯亲身实践的人。

intro.en: Armchair is an English compound, built from two native words.
intro.cn: armchair 是英语本土复合词，由两个本族语词拼成。

items.en: arm meant the limb of the body, from Proto-Germanic *armaz.
items.cn: arm 指身体的手臂，来自原始日耳曼语 *armaz（重构形式）。

items.en: chair came via Old French chaire from Latin cathedra, 'a seat'.
items.cn: chair 经古法语 chaire 来自拉丁语 cathedra，义为「座位」。

items.en: The compound armchair is first recorded in the 1600s for chairs with armrests.
items.cn: 复合词 armchair 首见于十七世纪，指带扶手的椅子。

items.en: The figurative sense grew in the 1800s: the armchair became the symbol of staying comfortably at home.
items.cn: 十九世纪出现比喻义：扶手椅成了足不出户、安逸旁观的象征。

items.en: The literal furniture sense is still the main one; the figurative use survives in set phrases.
items.cn: 字面的家具义仍是主义；比喻义保留在若干固定搭配中。

note.en: Words nearby in form are other compound chairs; words nearby in meaning describe comfort or sitting.
note.cn: 形近词多为其他复合家具词；近义词与舒适、就座相关。

entries.definition: the part of a chair where you rest your arm
entries.definitionCN: 椅子上供搁手臂的部分，即扶手；与 armchair 同含 arm 一词

entries.definition: a chair on wheels used by people who cannot walk
entries.definitionCN: 带轮子的椅子，供不能行走的人使用；同为 chair 复合词，结构平行
舰队；只是开头拼写 arm 相近，词源与 armchair 无关，来自西班牙语

entries.definition: a long comfortable seat for two or more people
entries.definitionCN: 供两人以上的长沙发；比 armchair 大，坐的人多

entries.definition: a long comfortable seat, the everyday word for sofa
entries.definitionCN: 长沙发的日常说法，与 sofa 基本同义

entries.definition: an armchair whose back can be tilted backwards
entries.definitionCN: 椅背可后仰的躺椅；可视为 armchair 的一种

normalIntro.en: Break the compound into its two native parts and picture the arms.
normalIntro.cn: 把复合词拆成两个本族语部分，想象出那两只「手臂」。

normal.en: arm + chair = a chair with arms.
normal.cn: arm（手臂）+ chair（椅子）＝带「手臂」的椅子，即扶手椅。

normal.en: The two armrests are the chair's arms hugging you.
normal.cn: 两条扶手就是椅子伸出来搂住你的两只手臂。

normal.en: Compare wheelchair: same pattern, chair named by its feature.
normal.cn: 对比 wheelchair（轮椅）：同一构词法，用特征命名椅子。

normal.en: An armchair traveller never leaves the chair, only reads.
normal.cn: armchair traveller（沙发旅行家）人不离椅，只靠阅读环游世界。

normal.en: Arm in arm, arm to armrest, arm to chair.
normal.cn: 由「手臂」顺藤摸瓜：手臂→扶手→带扶手的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture sinking into a big chair that embraces you with two arms.
abstract.cn: 想象陷进一把大椅子，它伸出两只手臂把你抱住。

abstract.en: The armchair is the throne of doing nothing.
abstract.cn: 扶手椅是「什么都不干」的王座，安逸旁观者的宝座。

abstract.en: From the armchair you can see the whole world on TV without moving.
abstract.cn: 坐在扶手椅里不用动，就能从电视里看遍全世界——空谈与远眺之位。

examples.en: She fell asleep in the armchair in front of the fire.
examples.cn: 她在壁炉前的扶手椅里睡着了。

examples.en: There is an old leather armchair in the corner of the study.
examples.cn: 书房角落里有一把旧皮扶手椅。

examples.en: Don't be an armchair critic; come and help us instead.
examples.cn: 别做空谈的批评家了，过来帮我们吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿姆切尔」——阿姆（arm，手臂）搭在椅儿（chair）上，扶手椅就是有两只手臂的椅子。

root: 英语本土复合词：arm（手臂，源自原始日耳曼语 *armaz，重构形式）+ chair（椅子，经古法语 chaire 来自拉丁语 cathedra「座位」）。字面即「带手臂的椅子」，指两侧有扶手。

sensesIntro.en: From the literal piece of furniture, the word extends to people who experience life only from that seat.
sensesIntro.cn: 从字面的家具义出发，引申指只坐在那把椅子上、不经实践便妄加评论或想象的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair with two arms that hold the sitter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把伸出两只手臂搂住坐者的椅子。

branches.en: The armrests give comfort, the seat invites you to sink in and stay.
branches.cn: 扶手带来舒适，座椅诱人陷进去不动。

branches.en: Staying seated means watching instead of doing.
branches.cn: 坐着不动，即旁观而非行动。

branches.en: From watching come opinions formed without experience.
branches.cn: 由旁观生出未经实践的意见。

branches.en: Both senses hinge on the picture of arms: the chair's and the metaphorical embrace of comfort.
branches.cn: 两个义项都系于「手臂」的画面：椅子的扶手，以及安逸的隐喻怀抱。

intro.en: Armchair is a native compound; the useful pieces are arm and chair and the pattern of naming a thing by its feature.
intro.cn: armchair 是本土复合词，可拆解的构件是 arm 与 chair，以及「以特征命名事物」的构词模式。

latinIntro.en: Only chair has a Latin ancestor; arm is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 chair 有拉丁祖先；arm 是日耳曼本族词。

items.meaning: arm of the body; hence armrest
a seat, naming the chair by its kind or feature
items.meaningCN: 椅子，作复合词后一部分，以种类或特征命名

items.meaning: a band worn around the arm
items.meaningCN: 戴在手臂上的带子，如袖章
items.example: The referee wore a red armband.

items.meaning: the part of the arm between elbow and wrist
items.meaningCN: 肘与腕之间的部分，前臂
items.example: He rolled up his sleeves to the forearm.

items.meaningCN: 军队；与 arm（手臂）词源无关，来自拉丁语 arma「武器」
items.example: He joined the army last year.

items.meaning: a chief church, from Latin cathedra 'seat' (of a bishop)
items.meaningCN: 大教堂；与 chair 同出拉丁语 cathedra「主教之座」
items.exampleCN: 我们参观了那座古老的大教堂。

items.meaning: with official authority, literally 'from the chair'
items.meaningCN: 以权威身份发言，字面义「自宝座上」
items.example: The professor spoke ex cathedra on the subject.
items.exampleCN: 教授以权威口吻谈论该问题。

items.meaning: the person presiding over a meeting
items.meaningCN: 主席；原指「坐椅子（主持）的人」

latinEntries.meaningCN: 座位；主教的宝座，是 chair 的最终来源

latinEntries.meaning: down + seat, a seat with a back
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一般认为由希腊语 kata（向下）+ hedra（座位）构成，指带靠背的座位

latinEntries.meaning: a seat, a place of sitting
latinEntries.meaningCN: 座位；拉丁语中与 hedra 同义的常用词

definition_en: the branch of a country's forces that fights on land, or a large group of people acting together
core_image: 成排的士兵在同一面旗下站定
scene: 村口的路上每天都有车队经过。The army set up a camp beside the river.
sceneCN: 这里 army 是「军队」（第 1 个义项：国家的陆上武装力量）；句意是军队在河边扎了营。

senses.title: The land forces of a country
senses.definition: the military force that operates on land
senses.definitionCN: 在陆地上作战的军事力量
senses.example: The army set up a camp beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 军队在河边扎了营。
senses.why: Old French armee meant 'an armed force', from arma, 'weapons'; the word names the body of armed men, not the weapons.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 armee 意为「武装力量」，源自 arma「武器」；这个词指武装起来的那群人，而不是武器本身。

senses.title: A large crowd acting together
senses.definition: a great number of people gathered for one purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为同一目的聚集起来的一大群人
senses.example: An army of volunteers cleared the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 一大群志愿者清理了海滩。
senses.why: The image of many people moving as one body transfers easily from soldiers to any organised crowd.
senses.whyCN: 许多人像一整个躯体那样一起行动，这一形象很容易从士兵移到任何有组织的群体。

senses.title: An organised body with a cause
senses.definition: a religious or charitable group with a military style
senses.definitionCN: 采用军事化形式的宗教或慈善团体
senses.example: The Salvation Army runs shelters across the city.
senses.exampleCN: 救世军在全市经营收容所。
senses.why: Groups that dress and march like soldiers borrow the name to signal discipline and mission.
senses.whyCN: 有些团体像士兵那样着装行进，便借这个词来表示纪律与使命。

intro.en: Army goes back to the Latin word for weapons.
intro.cn: army 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「武器」的词。

items.en: arma meant 'weapons, equipment of war'.
items.cn: arma 意为「武器、战具」。

items.en: armee meant 'an armed force'.
items.cn: armee 意为「武装力量」。

items.en: English army first meant a body of armed men.
items.cn: 英语 army 最初指一支武装起来的人马。

items.en: It settled as the name of the land force.
items.cn: 它固定为陆上武装力量的名称。

items.en: The crowd sense widened to volunteers and helpers.
items.cn: 「人群」义又扩展到志愿者与帮手。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the arma root; the near-meaning group names other fighting bodies.
note.cn: 形近组保留 arma 词根；近义组是其他作战队伍的名称。

normalIntro.en: An army is armed men, not the arms themselves.
normalIntro.cn: army 是武装起来的人，而不是武器本身。

normal.en: It usually takes the definite article: the army.
normal.cn: 它通常带定冠词：the army。

normal.en: An army of can describe any large crowd.
normal.cn: an army of 可以形容任何一大群人。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies.
normal.cn: 复数是把 y 变 i 再加 es。

normal.en: Army is the land force, not the navy.
normal.cn: army 指陆军，而非海军。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-my.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-my。

abstract.en: See rows of boots on wet ground.
abstract.cn: 想象湿地上成排的靴子。

abstract.en: See a flag raised over tents.
abstract.cn: 想象营帐上升起的旗。

abstract.en: See a long line of volunteers with bags.
abstract.cn: 想象提袋子的志愿者排成长线。

examples.en: The army set up a camp beside the river.
examples.cn: 军队在河边扎了营。

examples.en: An army of volunteers cleared the beach.
examples.cn: 一大群志愿者清理了海滩。

examples.en: The Salvation Army runs shelters across the city.
examples.cn: 救世军在全市经营收容所。

dict_mnemonic.text: arm（武器）加 -y：拿着武器的一群人，就是军队。

root: 来自拉丁语 arma「武器」，经古法语 armee「武装力量」进入英语；由「持武器的人群」引申为军队、大批人马与有组织的团体。

sensesIntro.en: Armed men become a land force, then any crowd that moves as one.
sensesIntro.cn: 持武器的人先成为陆上军队，再泛指任何整体行动的群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of soldiers standing under one flag.
core.cn: 核心意象：成排士兵站在同一面旗下。

intro.en: A French word of war that English made its own.
intro.cn: 这是一个来自法语的战争词，被英语完全吸收。

latinIntro.en: The weapon root arma also gives arm, armour and armament.
latinIntro.cn: 武器词根 arma 也派生出 arm、armour 与 armament。

definition_en: on every side of something, in various directions, or approximately
core_image: 绕着一样东西画一个整圈
scene: 孩子们跑到院子里四处张望。They sat around the fire and told stories.
sceneCN: 这里 around 是「围绕」（第 1 个义项：在某物的四周）；句意是他们围坐在火边讲故事。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：圆的，与 around 同源

senses.title: On every side of
senses.definition: surrounding something or positioned on its sides
senses.definitionCN: 环绕某物，或位于它的各侧
senses.example: They sat around the fire and told stories.
senses.exampleCN: 他们围坐在火边讲故事。
senses.why: Around is a- 'on' plus round; to be on the round of a thing is to be on its circle.
senses.whyCN: around 由 a-「在」与 round「圆」组成；处在某物的圆周上，就是在它四周。

senses.title: In various directions
senses.definition: moving from place to place without a fixed line
senses.definitionCN: 不沿固定路线而到处移动
senses.example: We walked around the old town all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们一上午都在老城里四处走。
senses.why: Circling a space means passing many points in it, so the word came to mean moving about freely.
senses.whyCN: 绕着一片空间走，就会经过其中许多点，于是这个词有了「四处走动」的意思。

senses.title: Approximately
senses.definition: used with numbers to give a rough figure
senses.definitionCN: 与数字连用，给出一个粗略的数目
senses.example: The trip takes around two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟行程大约要两小时。
senses.why: A rough figure circles the true one without landing on it, which is why around became a hedge for numbers.
senses.whyCN: 粗略的数字只是绕着真值转而没有落在上面，所以 around 也成了给数字留余地的说法。

intro.en: Around is a native compound of on and round.
intro.cn: around 是 on 与 round 构成的本族复合词。

items.en: rotundus meant 'round'.
items.cn: rotundus 意为「圆的」。

items.en: French rond gave English round.
items.cn: 法语 rond 给出英语 round。

items.en: The phrase on round meant 'in a circle'.
items.cn: 短语 on round 意为「成圈地」。

items.en: The two words fused into around.
items.cn: 两个词合成了 around。

items.en: The fused form added the senses 'about' and 'roughly'.
items.cn: 合并之后又添上「四处」与「大约」两义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the round root; the near-meaning group gives other words of surrounding and rough number.
note.cn: 形近组共享 round 词根；近义组是表示环绕与约数的其他词。

normalIntro.en: Around draws a circle and then fills it.
normalIntro.cn: around 先画一个圈，再把圈里走遍。

normal.en: Around the world means in many countries.
normal.cn: around the world 意为在世界各地。

normal.en: Look around is a fixed phrase for searching.
normal.cn: look around 是表示四处看的固定说法。

normal.en: With a number it means roughly.
normal.cn: 与数字连用时意为大约。

normal.en: American English often prefers around to round.
normal.cn: 美式英语常用 around 而非 round。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-ROUND.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-ROUND。

abstract.en: See a finger tracing a full circle.
abstract.cn: 想象手指画出一个整圈。

abstract.en: See footprints scattered in all directions.
abstract.cn: 想象脚印朝四处散开。

abstract.en: See a clock hand near but not on the hour.
abstract.cn: 想象时针靠近整点却未到整点。

examples.en: They sat around the fire and told stories.
examples.cn: 他们围坐在火边讲故事。

examples.en: We walked around the old town all morning.
examples.cn: 我们一上午都在老城里四处走。

examples.en: The trip takes around two hours.
examples.cn: 这趟行程大约要两小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（在）加 round（圆）：在圆周上，就是围绕；绕着走遍，就是到处。

root: 由 on 与 round 融合而成；round 源自拉丁语 rotundus「圆的」，经古法语 rond 进入英语。由「在圆周上」发展出围绕、四处与大约三义。

sensesIntro.en: A circle gives surrounding, then wandering, then a number that only circles the truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个圆先给出环绕，再给出遍游，最后给出只绕着真值转的约数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger drawing a complete circle in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指在空中画出一个完整的圆。

intro.en: A fused compound of a preposition and a Latin-derived adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个由介词与拉丁来源形容词融合而成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The round root rotundus also gives rotund and rotate.
latinIntro.cn: 圆词根 rotundus 也派生出 rotund 与 rotate。

definition_en: to plan and organise something, or to put things in a particular order
core_image: 把散乱的东西一件件摆成一行
scene: 桌上摊着十几份文件，他一份份摆好。She arranged the papers into three neat piles.
sceneCN: 这里 arrange 是「整理排列」（第 2 个义项：把东西按顺序摆好）；句意是她把文件理成了三摞整齐的纸。

senses.title: To plan an event
senses.definition: to make the necessary plans for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 为使某事发生而做好必要准备
senses.example: I have arranged a meeting for Monday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我已安排在周一上午开个会。
senses.why: Old French arengier meant 'to put in a row', and a row of steps in time is what a plan is.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 arengier 意为「排成一行」，而把步骤按时间排成一行，就是计划。

senses.title: To put in order
senses.definition: to place things in a chosen order or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 把物品按选定的顺序或样式摆放
senses.example: She arranged the papers into three neat piles.
senses.exampleCN: 她把文件理成了三摞整齐的纸。
senses.why: This is the literal row sense: objects are ranged so that their places make sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的「成行」义：物品被排好，使各自的位置合于秩序。

senses.title: To come to an agreement about
senses.definition: to settle details with someone in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先与某人把细节谈定
senses.example: We arranged for a taxi to meet us at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 我们安排了一辆出租车到机场接我们。
senses.why: Planning something with another person requires agreeing on the order of events, hence the sense of settling.
senses.whyCN: 与别人一起计划某事，必须先就事情的次序达成一致，于是产生「谈妥」义。

intro.en: Arrange comes from a French verb meaning 'to put in a row'.
intro.cn: arrange 来自一个意为「排成一行」的法语动词。

items.en: hring meant 'ring, circle, assembly'.
items.cn: hring 意为「环、圈、集会」。

items.en: rang meant 'row, line, rank'.
items.cn: rang 意为「行、列、排」。

items.en: arengier meant 'to set in a row'.
items.cn: arengier 意为「排成一行」。

items.en: English arrange kept the rowing sense and added planning.
items.cn: 英语 arrange 保留「排列」义，并添上「计划」义。

items.en: The word now covers both objects on a table and events in a calendar.
items.cn: 如今它既指桌上的物品，也指日程上的事情。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the range stem; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of ordering and planning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 range 词干；近义组是其他表示排序与计划的动词。

normalIntro.en: To arrange is to give things a row to stand in.
normalIntro.cn: arrange 就是给事物排出一行位置。

normal.en: Arrange for means to make preparations.
normal.cn: arrange for 意为做安排。

normal.en: Arrange a meeting is the common business phrase.
normal.cn: arrange a meeting 是常见的商务说法。

normal.en: The noun adds -ment.
normal.cn: 名词加 -ment。

normal.en: It is a regular verb with a soft g sound.
normal.cn: 它是规则动词，其中的 g 发软音。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-RRANGE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-RRANGE。

abstract.en: See books aligned along a shelf edge.
abstract.cn: 想象书沿架边排齐。

abstract.en: See a calendar with blocks filled in.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上被填满的格子。

abstract.en: See flowers placed one by one in a vase.
abstract.cn: 想象花一枝枝插进瓶里。

examples.en: I have arranged a meeting for Monday morning.
examples.cn: 我已安排在周一上午开个会。

examples.en: She arranged the papers into three neat piles.
examples.cn: 她把文件理成了三摞整齐的纸。

examples.en: We arranged for a taxi to meet us at the airport.
examples.cn: 我们安排了一辆出租车到机场接我们。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（向）加 range（行、列）：把东西排成行，就是排列；把事排进行程，就是安排。

root: 源自古法语 arengier「排成一行」，来自 rang「行、列」，更早可追至法兰克语 hring「环、圈」；由「排成行」发展出整理、安排与商定。

sensesIntro.en: A row of objects and a row of events are ordered by the same verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 排成一行的物品与排成一串的事情，用的是同一个动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: objects being set down one after another in a line.
core.cn: 核心意象：物件被一件接一件摆成一条线。

intro.en: A French verb of rowing that English widened to planning.
intro.cn: 这是一个法语「排列」动词，英语把它扩展到计划。

latinIntro.en: The row stem rang also gives range and rank.
latinIntro.cn: 行列词干 rang 也派生出 range 与 rank。

definition_zh: 安排；筹备；排列；布置；约定
definition_en: the act of planning something, the way things are laid out, or an agreement between people
core_image: 桌上的东西各就各位，形成一种秩序
scene: 婚礼前一天，所有人都在核对细节。The seating arrangement was changed twice.
sceneCN: 这里 arrangement 是「布置」（第 2 个义项：事物摆放的方式）；句意是座位安排改过两次。

senses.title: Plans made in advance
senses.definition: the preparations needed for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 为使某事发生所需的准备工作
senses.example: All the travel arrangements are in place.
senses.exampleCN: 所有出行安排都已就绪。
senses.why: The verb arrange meant to set things in a row, so the noun names the row of steps laid out before an event.
senses.whyCN: 动词 arrange 意为把事物排成行，名词便指事件之前排好的那一串步骤。

senses.title: The way things are laid out
senses.definition: the order or pattern in which objects are placed
senses.definitionCN: 物品被摆放成的那种顺序或样式
senses.example: The seating arrangement was changed twice.
senses.exampleCN: 座位安排改过两次。
senses.why: This is the noun at its most literal: the visible result of having ranged objects into places.
senses.whyCN: 这是该名词最字面的用法：把物品排到各自位置之后可见的结果。

senses.title: A settled agreement
senses.definition: an understanding reached between two sides
senses.definitionCN: 双方之间达成的谅解
senses.example: They have an arrangement with the landlord about the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他们和房东之间有关于房租的约定。
senses.why: When the rows being ordered are other people's interests, the result is a deal rather than a layout.
senses.whyCN: 当被排列的是彼此的利益时，排出来的结果就不是布置，而是协议。

intro.en: Arrangement is the noun of arrange, from a French verb of setting in rows.
intro.cn: arrangement 是 arrange 的名词，后者来自一个「排成行」的法语动词。

items.en: rang meant 'row, line, rank'.
items.cn: rang 意为「行、列、排」。

items.en: arengier meant 'to set in a row'.
items.cn: arengier 意为「排成一行」。

items.en: English arrange kept the ordering sense.
items.cn: 英语 arrange 保留了排列义。

items.en: arrangement added the sense of a settled plan.
items.cn: arrangement 又添上「议定的方案」一义。

items.en: The word now covers layout, preparations, and agreements.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖布置、筹备与约定三层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group is the arrange family; the near-meaning group gives plan, layout, and deal.
note.cn: 形近组是 arrange 词族；近义组分别给出计划、布局与协议。

normalIntro.en: An arrangement is a row that has been decided on.
normalIntro.cn: arrangement 就是已经定下来的那一行排列。

normal.en: Make arrangements is the plural idiom for preparing.
normal.cn: make arrangements 是表示筹备的复数习语。

normal.en: A seating arrangement describes who sits where.
normal.cn: seating arrangement 描述谁坐哪儿。

normal.en: By arrangement means after agreeing with someone.
normal.cn: by arrangement 意为经与某人商定。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二个音节。

normal.en: The verb behind it is arrange.
normal.cn: 其背后的动词是 arrange。

abstract.en: See name cards placed on a long table.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌上摆好的名牌。

abstract.en: See a list of steps ticked off.
abstract.cn: 想象一串步骤被逐条勾掉。

abstract.en: See two hands shaking over a paper.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在纸上方相握。

examples.en: All the travel arrangements are in place.
examples.cn: 所有出行安排都已就绪。

examples.en: The seating arrangement was changed twice.
examples.cn: 座位安排改过两次。

examples.en: They have an arrangement with the landlord about the rent.
examples.cn: 他们和房东之间有关于房租的约定。

dict_mnemonic.text: arrange（排列）加 -ment：排列出来的结果，就是布置；排好的步骤，就是安排。

root: 由动词 arrange 加名词后缀 -ment 构成；arrange 源自古法语 arengier「排成一行」，词根 rang 意为行列。

sensesIntro.en: Rows of objects give a layout, rows of steps give a plan, and rows of interests give a deal.
sensesIntro.cn: 物品排成行给出布置，步骤排成行给出计划，利益排成行给出协议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every object on a table sitting in its appointed place.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上每件东西都待在指定的位置。

intro.en: A noun of ordering that grew a sense of agreement.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示排序的名词，后来长出「协议」义。

latinIntro.en: The row stem rang also gives range and rank.
latinIntro.cn: 行列词干 rang 也派生出 range 与 rank。

definition_en: to take someone into legal custody, to stop something from continuing, or to hold attention
core_image: 一只手按住正在移动的肩膀
scene: 街角一阵骚动，警车停了下来。Police arrested two men near the station.
sceneCN: 这里 arrest 是「逮捕」（第 1 个义项：依法把人拘押）；句意是警察在车站附近逮捕了两名男子。

senses.title: To take into custody
senses.definition: to seize someone by legal authority
senses.definitionCN: 依法律权力把人抓起来
senses.example: Police arrested two men near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在车站附近逮捕了两名男子。
senses.why: Latin restare meant 'to stop, to remain'; ad plus restare gave 'to make someone stop', which law turned into detention.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 restare 意为「停住、留下」；ad 与它结合成「使人停下」，法律把这一动作定为拘押。

senses.title: To stop a process
senses.definition: to bring a movement or decline to a halt
senses.definitionCN: 使某种运动或下滑停住
senses.example: The new policy arrested the fall in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策遏止了销量的下滑。
senses.why: If arrest means to make something stop, it applies to trends as readily as to people.
senses.whyCN: 既然 arrest 意为使某物停下，它自然既能用于人，也能用于趋势。

senses.title: To hold attention
senses.definition: to make someone look and keep looking
senses.definitionCN: 使人看过去并一直看下去
senses.example: One painting arrested her attention at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 一幅画在门口就抓住了她的注意。
senses.why: Attention that is caught is held still, so the image of stopping a moving thing serves for the eye.
senses.whyCN: 被抓住的注意力会停住不动，于是「使移动之物停下」的形象正好用来形容目光。

intro.en: Arrest comes from Latin words meaning 'to stop and stay'.
intro.cn: arrest 来自意为「停住、留下」的拉丁词。

items.en: restare meant 'to remain, to stay back'.
items.cn: restare 意为「留下、停住」。

items.en: ad plus restare meant 'to stop something'.
items.cn: ad 与 restare 结合，意为「使某物停下」。

items.en: arester meant 'to halt, to detain'.
items.cn: arester 意为「使停下、扣留」。

items.en: English arrest first meant to stop a person or process.
items.cn: 英语 arrest 最初意为使人或过程停下。

items.en: Legal custody became the dominant sense.
items.cn: 依法拘押成为最主要的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same stem; the near-meaning group gives other words of holding and halting.
note.cn: 形近组同词干；近义组是其他表示扣留与止住的词。

normalIntro.en: Arrest means to bring a moving thing to a stop.
normalIntro.cn: arrest 就是让正在动的东西停下来。

normal.en: Under arrest is the fixed phrase for being held.
normal.cn: under arrest 是表示被拘押的固定说法。

normal.en: Police arrest someone for a crime.
normal.cn: 警察因某项罪行逮捕某人。

normal.en: The noun and the verb look the same.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形。

normal.en: Arresting can describe a striking face or idea.
normal.cn: arresting 可形容出众的面孔或想法。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-RREST.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-RREST。

abstract.en: See a hand closing on a shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扣住肩膀。

abstract.en: See a falling line flattened on a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象图上下滑的线被压平。

abstract.en: See a passer-by stopped by a painting.
abstract.cn: 想象路人被一幅画定住脚步。

examples.en: Police arrested two men near the station.
examples.cn: 警察在车站附近逮捕了两名男子。

examples.en: The new policy arrested the fall in sales.
examples.cn: 新政策遏止了销量的下滑。

examples.en: One painting arrested her attention at the door.
examples.cn: 一幅画在门口就抓住了她的注意。

dict_mnemonic.text: ar-（向）加 rest（停住）：让人或事物停下来，就是拦住；法律上拦住人，就是逮捕。

root: 来自拉丁语 adrestare「使停下」，由 ad 与 restare「停住、留下」构成，经古法语 arester 进入英语；由「止住」引申出逮捕、遏止与吸引注意。

sensesIntro.en: One stop covers a suspect, a falling trend, and a wandering eye.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「停下」既适用于嫌疑人，也适用于下滑的趋势和游移的目光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand stopping a moving shoulder.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按住移动中的肩膀。

intro.en: A Latin verb of stopping that law reshaped.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示止住的拉丁动词，法律重塑了它的用法。

latinIntro.en: The root restare, 'to stay', also gives rest and restaurant.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 restare「停留」也派生出 rest 与 restaurant。

definition_zh: 到达；到来；新来的人或物
definition_en: the act of reaching a place, the coming of an event, or a person or thing that has newly come
core_image: 门被推开，一个人提着行李走进来
scene: 大厅的屏幕上不断跳出新的班次。Her arrival was delayed by two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 arrival 是「到达」（第 1 个义项：抵达某地这一动作）；句意是她到达的时间推迟了两小时。

senses.title: The act of reaching a place
senses.definition: the moment of coming to a destination
senses.definitionCN: 来到目的地的那个时刻
senses.example: Her arrival was delayed by two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她到达的时间推迟了两小时。
senses.why: Latin ad ripam meant 'to the shore'; a ship reaching shore was the first kind of arrival.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad ripam 意为「到岸边」；船靠岸是最早的「到达」。

senses.title: The coming of an event
senses.definition: the beginning of a season, period, or change
senses.definitionCN: 某个季节、时期或变化开始出现
senses.example: The arrival of spring brought birds back to the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 春天的到来把鸟群带回了山谷。
senses.why: An event that was not here before now is here, so the word for reaching a place serves for reaching a time.
senses.whyCN: 原本不在此处的事件如今来了，于是「抵达某地」的词也用来指「抵达某个时刻」。

senses.title: A person or thing newly come
senses.definition: someone or something that has just joined a place
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚加入某个地方的人或物
senses.example: The new arrival was shown to her desk.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的人被领到了她的桌前。
senses.why: The abstract act turns concrete in speech: the arrival becomes the one who arrives.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的动作在口语里具体化了：arrival 变成了那个到达的人。

intro.en: Arrival is the noun of arrive, whose Latin source pictures a ship reaching shore.
intro.cn: arrival 是 arrive 的名词，其拉丁语来源描绘的是船靠岸。

items.en: ripa meant 'bank, shore'.
items.cn: ripa 意为「河岸、海岸」。

items.en: ad ripam meant 'to the shore'.
items.cn: ad ripam 意为「到岸边」。

items.en: ariver meant 'to come to shore'.
items.cn: ariver 意为「靠岸」。

items.en: English arrive widened from ships to any traveller.
items.cn: 英语 arrive 从船只扩展到任何旅行者。

items.en: arrival named both the reaching and the one who reached.
items.cn: arrival 既指抵达这一动作，也指抵达的人。

note.en: The look-alike group is the arrive family; the near-meaning group gives other words for coming.
note.cn: 形近组是 arrive 词族；近义组是其他表示到来的词。

normalIntro.en: Arrival is the boat touching the bank.
normalIntro.cn: arrival 就是船触到岸的那一刻。

normal.en: On arrival means as soon as one gets there.
normal.cn: on arrival 意为一到那里就。

normal.en: Airports split departures from arrivals.
normal.cn: 机场把出发与到达分作两处。

normal.en: A new arrival can be a baby or a package.
normal.cn: new arrival 可以是新生儿，也可以是新到的包裹。

normal.en: The verb drops the -al.
normal.cn: 动词形式去掉 -al。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-RRI-val.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-RRI-val。

abstract.en: See a suitcase set down in a doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象行李箱落在门口。

abstract.en: See a boat's bow touching a wooden pier.
abstract.cn: 想象船头碰到木码头。

abstract.en: See a board flipping to a new time.
abstract.cn: 想象显示牌翻出新的时间。

examples.en: Her arrival was delayed by two hours.
examples.cn: 她到达的时间推迟了两小时。

examples.en: The arrival of spring brought birds back to the valley.
examples.cn: 春天的到来把鸟群带回了山谷。

examples.en: The new arrival was shown to her desk.
examples.cn: 新来的人被领到了她的桌前。

dict_mnemonic.text: arrive（到达）加 -al：到达这件事，就是 arrival；也可指那个刚到的人。

root: 由动词 arrive 加 -al 构成；arrive 源自拉丁语 ad ripam「到岸边」，经古法语 ariver「靠岸」进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Reaching a place, reaching a season, and the one who reaches form one noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 抵达一个地方、抵达一个季节，以及抵达的那个人，共用一个名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway opening as a traveller steps in.
core.cn: 核心意象：门打开，旅人走进来。

intro.en: A noun made from a verb that first described ships.
intro.cn: 这是一个由最初描述船只的动词构成的名词。

latinIntro.en: The shore word ripa also gives riverbank and riparian.
latinIntro.cn: 表示岸的词 ripa 也派生出 riverbank 与 riparian。

definition_en: to reach a place, to come at a particular time, or to reach a decision
core_image: 脚步终于踏上目的地的地面
scene: 火车晚点了很久，站台上的人开始看表。They arrived just before the doors closed.
sceneCN: 这里 arrive 是「到达」（第 1 个义项：抵达某个地方）；句意是他们在门关上之前刚好赶到。

senses.title: To reach a place
senses.definition: to get to the end of a journey
senses.definitionCN: 走完一段路程来到终点
senses.example: They arrived just before the doors closed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门关上之前刚好赶到。
senses.why: Latin ad ripam, 'to the shore', described a ship touching land; English widened it to any journey's end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad ripam 意为「到岸边」，本指船靠岸；英语把它扩展到任何旅程的终点。

senses.title: To come at a point in time
senses.definition: to occur at last, of a moment or event
senses.definitionCN: 某个时刻或事件终于发生
senses.example: The day of the exam finally arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 考试那天终于到了。
senses.why: Time is pictured as a road, so a date can reach us just as a traveller does.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一条路，所以一个日期也能像旅人一样走到我们面前。

senses.title: To reach a conclusion
senses.definition: to settle on a decision after discussion
senses.definitionCN: 经过讨论后定下某个决定
senses.example: The committee arrived at a compromise.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会达成了一个折中方案。
senses.why: A decision is a destination in reasoning, so reaching it borrows the language of travel.
senses.whyCN: 决定是推理路上的目的地，所以抵达决定也借用了旅行的说法。

intro.en: Arrive began as a word about ships coming to shore.
intro.cn: arrive 最初是一个关于船靠岸的词。

items.en: ripa meant 'bank, shore'.
items.cn: ripa 意为「岸」。

items.en: The phrase meant 'to the shore'.
items.cn: 这一短语意为「到岸边」。

items.en: ariver meant 'to come to land'.
items.cn: ariver 意为「靠岸」。

items.en: English arrive extended to travellers by land.
items.cn: 英语 arrive 扩展到陆上的旅行者。

items.en: The word also covers the coming of events and decisions.
items.cn: 这个词也涵盖事件与决定的到来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the arrive family; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of reaching.
note.cn: 形近组是 arrive 词族；近义组是其他表示抵达的动词。

normalIntro.en: To arrive is to end a journey at a place.
normalIntro.cn: arrive 就是把旅程结束在某个地方。

normal.en: Use arrive in for cities and countries.
normal.cn: 到达城市和国家时用 arrive in。

normal.en: Use arrive at for stations and decisions.
normal.cn: 到达车站或作出决定时用 arrive at。

normal.en: It never takes a direct place object: no arrive the station.
normal.cn: 它后面不能直接接地点宾语。

normal.en: The noun is arrival.
normal.cn: 名词是 arrival。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-RRIVE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-RRIVE。

abstract.en: See feet stepping onto a platform.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚踩上站台。

abstract.en: See a calendar page turned at last.
abstract.cn: 想象日历终于翻到那一页。

abstract.en: See hands meeting over a settled paper.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在定稿上方相合。

examples.en: They arrived just before the doors closed.
examples.cn: 他们在门关上之前刚好赶到。

examples.en: The day of the exam finally arrived.
examples.cn: 考试那天终于到了。

examples.en: The committee arrived at a compromise.
examples.cn: 委员会达成了一个折中方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: ar-（向）加 rive（岸）：船向岸边靠过去，就是到达。

root: 源自拉丁语 ad ripam「到岸边」，经古法语 ariver「靠岸」进入英语；由船靠岸扩展到一切抵达，再引申为时刻到来与达成决定。

sensesIntro.en: A traveller, a date, and a decision all can be reached.
sensesIntro.cn: 旅人、日期与决定，都可以被「抵达」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot landing on the far bank.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚落在对岸。

intro.en: A verb of landing that now covers any kind of arrival.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示靠岸的动词，如今涵盖各种到达。

latinIntro.en: The shore word ripa also gives riparian.
latinIntro.cn: 表示岸的词 ripa 也派生出 riparian。

definition_en: a thin stick with a pointed head shot from a bow, or a sign shaped like one
core_image: 一支箭离弦飞出，指向远方
scene: 靶场上风很大，弦声一响就看不见了。The arrow struck the outer ring of the target.
sceneCN: 这里 arrow 是「箭」（第 1 个义项：用弓射出的带尖头的细杆）；句意是那支箭射中了靶的外圈。

senses.title: A weapon shot from a bow
senses.definition: a slender shaft with a point, driven by a bowstring
senses.definitionCN: 由弓弦推动的细长带尖杆状物
senses.example: The arrow struck the outer ring of the target.
senses.exampleCN: 那支箭射中了靶的外圈。
senses.why: Old English earh and Old Norse or both named this weapon; the English form settled as arrow.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 earh 与古诺斯语 or 都指这件武器；英语的形式最终定为 arrow。

senses.title: A sign pointing the way
senses.definition: a mark or symbol shaped like an arrow
senses.definitionCN: 形状像箭的标记或符号
senses.example: A white arrow on the road showed us where to turn.
senses.exampleCN: 路面上一个白色箭头告诉我们该往哪里转。
senses.why: The weapon's straight flight toward a mark made it the natural picture for direction.
senses.whyCN: 箭笔直飞向目标，这一形象自然成了方向的图示。

intro.en: Arrow is one of the oldest words English has for a weapon.
intro.cn: arrow 是英语中表示武器的最古老的词之一。

items.en: or meant 'arrow' in the northern tongue.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 or 意为「箭」。

items.en: earh was the native English noun for an arrow.
items.cn: earh 是英语本族表示箭的名词。

items.en: The two forms merged into arwe.
items.cn: 两种形式合并为 arwe。

items.en: The modern spelling arrow became fixed.
items.cn: 现代拼写 arrow 固定下来。

items.en: The shape of the weapon gave the road sign its name.
items.cn: 武器的形状使路标也用上了这个词。

note.en: The look-alike group builds on the same noun; the near-meaning group gives other pointed missiles and markers.
note.cn: 形近组由同一名词构成；近义组是其他尖锐投射物与标记。

normalIntro.en: An arrow is a line that ends in a point.
normalIntro.cn: arrow 就是一条末端成尖的线。

normal.en: Bow and arrow is a fixed pair.
normal.cn: bow and arrow 是固定搭配。

normal.en: Road signs use arrows to show turns.
normal.cn: 路标用箭头表示转弯。

normal.en: The plural is arrows.
normal.cn: 复数是 arrows。

normal.en: On a keyboard the arrow keys move the cursor.
normal.cn: 键盘上的方向键移动光标。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-row.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-row。

abstract.en: See a string released and a shaft flying.
abstract.cn: 想象弓弦松开、箭飞出去。

abstract.en: See a white chevron painted on asphalt.
abstract.cn: 想象沥青上画着的白色箭形。

abstract.en: See a hand pointing firmly at a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手坚定地指向门口。

examples.en: The arrow struck the outer ring of the target.
examples.cn: 那支箭射中了靶的外圈。

examples.en: A white arrow on the road showed us where to turn.
examples.cn: 路面上一个白色箭头告诉我们该往哪里转。

examples.en: He drew the bow and let the arrow fly.
examples.cn: 他拉满弓，把箭射了出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 arrow 想成一条笔直的线加一个尖：既是射出的箭，也是指路的箭头。

root: 源自古英语 earh 与古诺斯语 or，中古英语作 arwe，后固定为 arrow；由武器义引申为指示方向的箭头符号。

sensesIntro.en: A straight flight toward a mark became the sign that shows a way.
sensesIntro.cn: 直奔目标的飞行，成了指引方向的符号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shaft leaving the string and cutting forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭离弦向前穿出。

intro.en: A Germanic weapon word with very few derivatives.
intro.cn: 这是一个日耳曼语系的武器词，派生词很少。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin root; its compounds are all English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，其复合词都由英语自身构成。

definition_zh: 艺术；美术；技艺；人文学科
definition_en: creative work such as painting or music, a skilled way of doing something, or the humanities
core_image: 画布上第一笔颜色落下
scene: 展厅里人不多，光线落在墙面上。She has studied art since she was a child.
sceneCN: 这里 art 是「美术」（第 1 个义项：绘画雕塑等创造性作品与活动）；句意是她从小就在学美术。

pos.zh: 名词：艺术；技艺；人文学科

senses.title: Creative work
senses.definition: painting, sculpture, music and similar forms of expression
senses.definitionCN: 绘画、雕塑、音乐等表达形式
senses.example: She has studied art since she was a child.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小就在学美术。
senses.why: Latin ars meant 'skill'; the skill of making beautiful things became the name of the things made.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ars 意为「技艺」；制作美的事物的技艺，后来成了这些事物本身的名称。

senses.title: A skilled way of doing
senses.definition: a practiced ability in some activity
senses.definitionCN: 在某种活动中练就的本领
senses.example: Letter writing is a lost art.
senses.exampleCN: 写信是一门失传的技艺。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: any craft that requires trained skill is an art.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一义：任何需要训练有素的技能的手艺都叫艺术。

senses.title: The humanities
senses.definition: subjects such as history and literature, in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 历史、文学等学科，通常用复数
senses.example: He took a degree in the arts.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿的是人文学科学位。
senses.why: Medieval universities grouped the verbal and moral studies as arts, a use that still names whole faculties.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪大学把语言与伦理类学问归为「艺」，这一用法至今仍用来指整个学部。

intro.en: Art is a short Latin word for skill that widened to beauty.
intro.cn: art 是一个简短的拉丁语「技艺」词，后来扩展到美。

items.en: ars meant 'skill, craft, method'.
items.cn: ars 意为「技能、手艺、方法」。

items.en: The accusative artem carried the word into French.
items.cn: 宾格形式 artem 把词带入法语。

items.en: art kept the sense of trained skill.
items.cn: 法语 art 保留了「训练所得的技能」义。

items.en: English art first meant learning and craft.
items.cn: 英语 art 最初指学问与手艺。

items.en: The fine arts gave the word its modern centre.
items.cn: 美术使这个词的重心移到了今天的位置。

note.en: The look-alike group is the art family; the near-meaning group gives skill and craft.
note.cn: 形近组是 art 词族；近义组是技能与手艺。

normalIntro.en: Art begins as skill and ends as beauty.
normalIntro.cn: art 从技艺开始，到美结束。

normal.en: The plural arts often means the humanities.
normal.cn: 复数 arts 常指人文学科。

normal.en: The art of doing something is a common phrase.
normal.cn: the art of 加动名词是常见说法。

normal.en: Work of art is countable and takes an article.
normal.cn: work of art 可数，前面要加冠词。

normal.en: Artful can be a warning word, meaning crafty.
normal.cn: artful 有时带贬义，意为狡黠。

normal.en: The word is one long open vowel: ART.
normal.cn: 这个词只有一个长元音：ART。

abstract.en: See a brush loaded with colour above canvas.
abstract.cn: 想象蘸满颜料的笔停在画布上方。

abstract.en: See hands shaping clay on a wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在转盘上塑泥。

abstract.en: See a gallery wall lit from one side.
abstract.cn: 想象展厅墙面被一侧的光照亮。

examples.en: She has studied art since she was a child.
examples.cn: 她从小就在学美术。

examples.en: Letter writing is a lost art.
examples.cn: 写信是一门失传的技艺。

examples.en: He took a degree in the arts.
examples.cn: 他拿的是人文学科学位。

dict_mnemonic.text: art 本是「技艺」：把一件事做到有章法、有美感，就成了艺术。

root: 来自拉丁语 ars「技能、手艺」，宾格 artem 经法语 art 进入英语；由「训练所得的技艺」发展出美术、技巧与人文学科诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Skill produces beautiful things, and the name of the skill becomes the name of the faculty.
sensesIntro.cn: 技艺造出美的东西，技艺之名又成了整个学部的名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a first stroke of colour laid on a blank canvas.
core.cn: 核心意象：空白画布上落下的第一笔颜色。

intro.en: A Latin word of skill whose family fills the museum and the workshop.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示技艺的拉丁词，其词族遍布美术馆与作坊。

latinIntro.en: The root ars also gives artful, artifice, and artisan through French.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ars 经法语也派生出 artful、artifice 与 artisan。

definition_en: a piece of writing in a newspaper, a single object, a word like the or a, or a clause in a document
core_image: 一份文字被分成一段一段的小节
scene: 早餐桌上摊着刚送来的报纸。She read an article about the harbour project.
sceneCN: 这里 article 是「文章」（第 1 个义项：报刊上的一篇文字）；句意是她读了一篇关于港口工程的报道。

pos.zh: 名词：文章；物品；冠词；条款

derivatives.zh: 动词：清楚表达，同出 articulus 一词

senses.title: A piece of writing
senses.definition: a short piece published in a paper or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 发表在报纸或杂志上的短篇文字
senses.example: She read an article about the harbour project.
senses.exampleCN: 她读了一篇关于港口工程的报道。
senses.why: Latin articulus meant 'a small joint or part'; a published piece is one part of a larger paper.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 articulus 意为「小关节、小部分」；一篇刊出的文字正是整份报纸的一个部分。

senses.title: A single item
senses.definition: one particular thing among others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物中的某一件
senses.example: Every article of clothing was packed in paper.
senses.exampleCN: 每件衣物都用纸包好了。
senses.why: An item is a distinct part of a set, exactly what the 'small joint' image suggests.
senses.whyCN: 一件物品是整套东西中独立的一部分，正合「小关节」的形象。

senses.title: A grammatical word
senses.definition: a word such as the or a placed before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前的小词，如 the 或 a
senses.example: English uses the article more often than Chinese does.
senses.exampleCN: 英语使用冠词的频率比汉语高。
senses.why: Old grammarians called these little words articles because each was a small joint attaching to a noun.
senses.whyCN: 古代语法学家把这些小词叫作 article，因为它们像小关节一样附着在名词上。

senses.title: A clause in a document
senses.definition: one numbered section of a treaty or law
senses.definitionCN: 条约或法律中编号的一节
senses.example: The treaty was signed under article four.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约是依据第四条签署的。
senses.why: Legal texts are divided into numbered parts, and each part is a joint of the whole document.
senses.whyCN: 法律文本被分成编号的若干部分，每一部分都是整份文件的一个关节。

intro.en: Article comes from a Latin word for a small joint.
intro.cn: article 来自一个意为「小关节」的拉丁词。

items.en: artus meant 'joint, limb'.
items.cn: artus 意为「关节、肢体」。

items.en: articulus was the diminutive, 'a little joint'.
items.cn: articulus 是其指小形式，意为「小关节」。

items.en: article meant 'a division, a clause'.
items.cn: article 意为「一个部分、一条款」。

items.en: English used it for clauses and for items.
items.cn: 英语用它指条款与物品。

items.en: Journalism gave it the sense of a published piece.
items.cn: 新闻业赋予了它「刊出文章」这一义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the articulus root; the near-meaning group gives other words for a written piece and an item.
note.cn: 形近组共享 articulus 词根；近义组是其他表示文字篇章与单件的词。

normalIntro.en: An article is a small part cut from something larger.
normalIntro.cn: article 就是从更大的东西上切下来的一个小部分。

normal.en: The definite article is the, the indefinite one is a.
normal.cn: 定冠词是 the，不定冠词是 a。

normal.en: An article of clothing counts single items.
normal.cn: an article of clothing 用来数单件衣物。

normal.en: Legal texts number their articles.
normal.cn: 法律文本会把条款编号。

normal.en: The verb form is articulate.
normal.cn: 其动词形式是 articulate。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-ti-cle.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-ti-cle。

abstract.en: See a page folded into sections.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被折成几段。

abstract.en: See a short word slipping in before a noun.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小词滑到名词前面。

abstract.en: See a coat laid out as one item.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套作为单件摆着。

examples.en: She read an article about the harbour project.
examples.cn: 她读了一篇关于港口工程的报道。

examples.en: Every article of clothing was packed in paper.
examples.cn: 每件衣物都用纸包好了。

examples.en: The treaty was signed under article four.
examples.cn: 该条约是依据第四条签署的。

dict_mnemonic.text: artic（关节）加 -le（小）：一个小关节，就是一节、一件、一条，也可以是一篇文章。

root: 来自拉丁语 articulus「小关节」，是 artus「关节」的指小形式；由「一段、一节」发展出条款、物品、文章与冠词诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense is a joint: a part of a paper, a set, a sentence, or a law.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是一个关节：报纸的一节、一套的一件、句子的一节、法律的一条。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long text marked off into numbered parts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一篇长文被划成若干编号的部分。

intro.en: A Latin diminutive of 'joint' that spread through law, grammar, and news.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁语「关节」的指小词，遍布法律、语法与新闻。

latinIntro.en: The joint root artus also gives articulate and arthritis.
latinIntro.cn: 关节词根 artus 也派生出 articulate 与 arthritis。

definition_zh: 人造的；人工的；虚假的；做作的
definition_en: made by people rather than nature, or not genuine in manner
core_image: 温室里用支架撑起来的花
scene: 花店里那束花摸起来有点硬。These flowers are artificial and never need water.
sceneCN: 这里 artificial 是「人造的」（第 1 个义项：非自然生成，由人制造）；句意是这些花是人造的，从不需要浇水。

senses.title: Made by people
senses.definition: produced by human work rather than occurring naturally
senses.definitionCN: 由人力制造而非自然生成
senses.example: These flowers are artificial and never need water.
senses.exampleCN: 这些花是人造的，从不需要浇水。
senses.why: Latin artificium meant 'craftsmanship', from ars 'skill' and facere 'to make'; the artificial is what skill makes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 artificium 意为「手艺」，由 ars「技艺」与 facere「制作」构成；人造之物正是技艺所做。

senses.title: Not genuine in manner
senses.definition: put on for effect and lacking real feeling
senses.definitionCN: 为效果而装出来的，缺乏真实情感
senses.example: His artificial smile fooled no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他做作的笑容骗不了任何人。
senses.why: If a thing is made rather than grown, a feeling that is made rather than felt is artificial too.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西是造出来的而不是长出来的，那么装出来的而非真切感受到的情绪也是 artificial。

intro.en: Artificial belongs to the Latin family of skill and making.
intro.cn: artificial 属于拉丁语中表示技艺与制作的那一族词。

items.en: ars meant 'skill, craft'.
items.cn: ars 意为「技艺、手艺」。

items.en: facere meant 'to make, to do'.
items.cn: facere 意为「制作、做」。

items.en: artificium meant 'craftsmanship, a made thing'.
items.cn: artificium 意为「手艺、制作之物」。

items.en: artificialis meant 'made by art'.
items.cn: artificialis 意为「由技艺制成的」。

items.en: English artificial first meant skilfully made, then not natural.
items.cn: 英语 artificial 先指「制作精巧的」，后指「非自然的」。

note.en: The look-alike group comes from the same making root; the near-meaning group gives other words for not natural.
note.cn: 形近组同出「制作」词根；近义组是其他表示非自然的词。

normalIntro.en: Artificial means skill made it, not nature.
normalIntro.cn: artificial 意为由技艺造出，而非自然生成。

normal.en: Artificial intelligence is the modern headline use.
normal.cn: 人工智能是当代最醒目的用法。

normal.en: Artificial light contrasts with daylight.
normal.cn: artificial light 与日光相对。

normal.en: Applied to people, it means put on.
normal.cn: 用于人时，意为装出来的。

normal.en: The adverb is artificially.
normal.cn: 副词是 artificially。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: ar-ti-FI-cial.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：ar-ti-FI-cial。

abstract.en: See plastic petals catching the light.
abstract.cn: 想象塑料花瓣反着光。

abstract.en: See a lamp standing in for the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯代替太阳。

abstract.en: See a smile held a moment too long.
abstract.cn: 想象一个停留得过久的微笑。

examples.en: These flowers are artificial and never need water.
examples.cn: 这些花是人造的，从不需要浇水。

examples.en: His artificial smile fooled no one.
examples.cn: 他做作的笑容骗不了任何人。

examples.en: The lake is kept full by artificial means.
examples.cn: 这个湖靠人工方式保持水量。

dict_mnemonic.text: arti（技艺）加 fici（做）加 -al：用技艺做出来的，就是人造的。

root: 来自拉丁语 artificialis「由技艺制成的」，由 ars「技艺」与 facere「制作」构成；由「人工制造」引申为「不自然、做作」。

sensesIntro.en: What skill makes instead of nature grows is artificial, and so is a feeling put on.
sensesIntro.cn: 由技艺造出而非自然长成的是人造的，装出来的情感也是。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flower held up by a hidden wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一朵由暗线撑起的花。

intro.en: A Latin adjective joining skill with making.
intro.cn: 这是一个把技艺与制作结合起来的拉丁形容词。

latinIntro.en: The making root facere also gives factory, effect, and difficult.
latinIntro.cn: 制作词根 facere 也派生出 factory、effect 与 difficult。

definition_zh: 艺术家；画家；表演者；能手
definition_en: a person who creates art, performs, or does something with great skill
core_image: 衣袖沾着颜料，手里握着画笔
scene: 画室的窗开着，颜料味很重。The artist worked standing up for six hours.
sceneCN: 这里 artist 是「画家」（第 1 个义项：从事绘画等造型艺术的人）；句意是这位画家站着画了六个小时。

pos.zh: 名词：艺术家；表演者；能手

senses.title: A maker of visual art
senses.definition: someone who paints, draws, or makes sculpture
senses.definitionCN: 从事绘画或雕塑创作的人
senses.example: The artist worked standing up for six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家站着画了六个小时。
senses.why: French artiste came from Latin ars, 'skill'; the word first named anyone skilled, then those skilled in art.
senses.whyCN: 法语 artiste 源自拉丁语 ars「技艺」；这个词先指任何有技艺的人，后专指艺术上有技艺的人。

senses.title: A performer
senses.definition: a singer, dancer, or actor who performs for an audience
senses.definitionCN: 为观众表演的歌手、舞者或演员
senses.example: The artist came back for a second song.
senses.exampleCN: 这位歌手返场又唱了一首。
senses.why: Music and stage work are also arts, so the performer is an artist in the same old sense of trained skill.
senses.whyCN: 音乐与舞台同样是艺术，所以表演者仍是「有训练技艺之人」这一古老意义上的艺术家。

senses.title: Someone very skilled
senses.definition: a person who does something with unusual skill
senses.definitionCN: 把某事做得格外有本领的人
senses.example: He is an artist at finding cheap flights.
senses.exampleCN: 他找便宜机票是个高手。
senses.why: Since art once meant any craft, calling someone an artist praises the skill rather than the medium.
senses.whyCN: 既然 art 本指任何手艺，称某人为 artist 就是在夸技艺，而非指门类。

intro.en: Artist came to English through French and Italian from the Latin word for skill.
intro.cn: artist 经法语与意大利语进入英语，源头是拉丁语的「技艺」一词。

items.en: ars meant 'skill, craft'.
items.cn: ars 意为「技艺、手艺」。

items.en: artista named a skilled maker or scholar.
items.cn: artista 指有技艺的制作者或学者。

items.en: artiste carried the word into French.
items.cn: artiste 把词带入法语。

items.en: English artist first meant a master of any craft.
items.cn: 英语 artist 最初指任何手艺的行家。

items.en: The word narrowed to painters and then widened to performers.
items.cn: 这个词先缩小到画家，后又扩展到表演者。

note.en: The look-alike group is the art family; the near-meaning group names other makers and performers.
note.cn: 形近组是 art 词族；近义组是其他创作者与表演者。

normalIntro.en: An artist is anyone whose skill shows in what they make.
normalIntro.cn: artist 就是技艺体现在作品里的人。

normal.en: In music, artist means a recording performer.
normal.cn: 音乐语境里，artist 指录制作品的表演者。

normal.en: Con artist has nothing to do with art.
normal.cn: con artist 与艺术无关，指骗子。

normal.en: The noun artistry means artistic skill.
normal.cn: 名词 artistry 意为艺术才能。

normal.en: The plural is artists.
normal.cn: 复数是 artists。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-tist.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-tist。

abstract.en: See a brush held loosely between fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象手指间松松握着画笔。

abstract.en: See a stage lit from below.
abstract.cn: 想象被下方灯光照亮的舞台。

abstract.en: See a hand steadying a small sculpture.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手稳住小雕像。

examples.en: The artist worked standing up for six hours.
examples.cn: 这位画家站着画了六个小时。

examples.en: The artist came back for a second song.
examples.cn: 这位歌手返场又唱了一首。

examples.en: He is an artist at finding cheap flights.
examples.cn: 他找便宜机票是个高手。

dict_mnemonic.text: art（艺术）加 -ist（人）：从事艺术的人，就是艺术家。

root: 经法语 artiste 与意大利语 artista 来自拉丁语 ars「技艺」；由「有技艺之人」窄化为造型艺术家，又扩展到表演者与能手。

sensesIntro.en: Skill in making, skill on stage, and skill anywhere share one word.
sensesIntro.cn: 制作中的技艺、舞台上的技艺、任何行当的技艺，共用同一个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding a brush above wet paint.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握着笔停在未干的颜料上。

intro.en: A French and Italian word built on the Latin root for skill.
intro.cn: 这是一个经法语与意大利语构成、以拉丁语「技艺」为根的词。

latinIntro.en: The root ars also gives art, artifice, and artisan.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ars 也派生出 art、artifice 与 artisan。

definition_en: used to show a role, a comparison, a point in time, or a reason
core_image: 一条线把两件事并排连起来
scene: 她在医院里穿着白衣，走过长廊。She works as a nurse in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 as 是「作为」（第 1 个义项：表示身份或角色）；句意是她在城里当护士。

derivatives.zh: 副词：也，与 as 同出一个古英语复合词

senses.title: In the role of
senses.definition: used to name the job or function of someone
senses.definitionCN: 用来指明某人的职业或功能
senses.example: She works as a nurse in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她在城里当护士。
senses.why: Old English alswa meant 'all so, just so'; from 'in that way' came the sense 'in the capacity of'.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 alswa 意为「正如此、就这样」；由「以那种方式」发展出「以那个身份」。

senses.title: In the same degree as
senses.definition: used to compare two things as equal
senses.definitionCN: 用来比较两件事程度相同
senses.example: He is as tall as his brother.
senses.exampleCN: 他和他哥哥一样高。
senses.why: If as means 'just so', placing it on both sides of an adjective says the two sides are just so alike.
senses.whyCN: 既然 as 意为「正是如此」，把它放在形容词两边，就是说两边同样如此。

senses.title: At the time when
senses.definition: used to introduce an action happening at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 引出与主句同时发生的动作
senses.example: As I left, the phone rang.
senses.exampleCN: 我离开的时候，电话响了。
senses.why: Two events happening 'just so' together are simultaneous, which gives the time sense.
senses.whyCN: 两件事「正好这样」同时发生，就是同时性，于是产生时间义。

senses.title: Because
senses.definition: used to give the reason for something
senses.definitionCN: 用来给出某事的原因
senses.example: As it was late, we took a taxi.
senses.exampleCN: 因为时间晚了，我们打了车。
senses.why: A circumstance that stands 'just so' alongside an act is often its cause, so as came to introduce reasons.
senses.whyCN: 与行为「正好并列」的情境往往就是它的原因，于是 as 也用来引出理由。

intro.en: As is a worn-down form of an Old English phrase meaning 'all so'.
intro.cn: as 是古英语中意为「完全如此」的短语磨损后的形式。

items.en: alswa meant 'all so, wholly so'.
items.cn: alswa 意为「完全如此」。

items.en: The word shortened to als and then as.
items.cn: 这个词缩短为 als，再变为 as。

items.en: As spread into comparisons and time clauses.
items.cn: as 扩展到比较与时间从句。

items.en: The reason sense became common in writing.
items.cn: 原因义在书面语中变得常见。

items.en: As is now one of the commonest words in English.
items.cn: 如今 as 是英语中最常用的词之一。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the old 'so' family; the near-meaning group gives words that cover single senses of as.
note.cn: 形近组同出古英语「如此」一族；近义组是分别承担 as 某一义项的词。

normalIntro.en: As points at a role, a match, a moment, or a cause.
normalIntro.cn: as 分别指向身份、相同、时刻与原因。

normal.en: As a teacher names the job.
normal.cn: as a teacher 点明职业。

normal.en: As tall as repeats the word for comparison.
normal.cn: as tall as 重复该词以作比较。

normal.en: As I left marks two things happening together.
normal.cn: as I left 表示两事同时发生。

normal.en: As can also mean because at the start of a clause.
normal.cn: 置于句首时 as 也可表示因为。

normal.en: The word is weak in speech: /əz/.
normal.cn: 口语中它读得轻：/əz/。

abstract.en: See two lines laid exactly parallel.
abstract.cn: 想象两条完全平行的线。

abstract.en: See a name tag pinned to a shirt.
abstract.cn: 想象别在衬衫上的名牌。

abstract.en: See two clocks showing the same minute.
abstract.cn: 想象两个时钟指着同一分钟。

examples.en: She works as a nurse in the city.
examples.cn: 她在城里当护士。

examples.en: As I left, the phone rang.
examples.cn: 我离开的时候，电话响了。

examples.en: As it was late, we took a taxi.
examples.cn: 因为时间晚了，我们打了车。

dict_mnemonic.text: as 的核心是「就这样」：是身份、是相同、是同时，也是原因。

root: 源自古英语 alswa「完全如此」，中古英语缩为 als 再变为 as；由「正是这样」发展出身份、比较、时间与原因四种用法。

sensesIntro.en: One small word says: in that role, to that degree, at that moment, for that reason.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个小词同时表示：以那个身份、到那个程度、在那个时刻、由于那个原因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line joining two things that stand level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线把两件并排而立的事物连起来。

intro.en: A function word with almost no derivational life of its own.
intro.cn: 这是一个功能词，本身几乎不派生新词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element; the whole history is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁成分，整段历史都属于日耳曼语。

definition_en: the grey powder left after something burns, or a tall tree with hard pale wood
core_image: 火熄之后，灶底剩下一层细白的灰
scene: 壁炉里的木柴烧了整夜，早上只剩下粉末。The fire had left a layer of ash on the stones.
sceneCN: 这里 ash 是「灰烬」（第 1 个义项：燃烧后剩下的粉末）；句意是炉火在石面上留下了一层灰。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：覆着灰的；灰似的

senses.title: Powder left by fire
senses.definition: the soft grey remains of something that has burned
senses.definitionCN: 某物燃烧后留下的松软灰色残余
senses.example: The fire had left a layer of ash on the stones.
senses.exampleCN: 炉火在石面上留下了一层灰。
senses.why: Old English asce named the burnt powder, and the word has kept that sense for a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 asce 指燃烧后的粉末，这个词一千年来都保留着这一义。

senses.title: A tall hardwood tree
senses.definition: a tree with pale strong wood and winged seeds
senses.definitionCN: 木质浅色坚硬、结翅果的高大树木
senses.example: An old ash stands at the corner of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 田地角上立着一棵老白蜡树。
senses.why: This is a different Old English word, aesc, which happened to fall together in spelling and sound.
senses.whyCN: 这其实是另一个古英语词 aesc，只是拼写与读音后来与「灰」合流了。

intro.en: Ash joins two Old English words that came to look alike.
intro.cn: ash 合并了两个原本不同、后来形貌相近的古英语词。

items.en: asce meant 'ash, burnt powder'.
items.cn: asce 意为「灰、燃烧后的粉末」。

items.en: aesc meant 'ash tree' and also named the rune for it.
items.cn: aesc 意为「白蜡树」，也指代表它的卢恩字母。

items.en: Both words settled into the spelling asshe.
items.cn: 两个词都归入拼写 asshe。

items.en: The modern spelling ash became standard.
items.cn: 现代拼写 ash 成为标准。

items.en: The tree sense survives mainly in wood and plant names.
items.cn: 树木义主要保留在木材与植物名称中。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ash family; the near-meaning group gives other burnt remains.
note.cn: 形近组是 ash 词族；近义组是其他燃烧残余。

normalIntro.en: Ash is what fire leaves behind.
normalIntro.cn: ash 就是火留下的东西。

normal.en: The burnt sense is usually uncountable.
normal.cn: 「灰烬」义通常不可数。

normal.en: Ashes in the plural can mean a person's remains.
normal.cn: 复数 ashes 可指人的骨灰。

normal.en: The tree sense survives in ash wood.
normal.cn: 树木义保留在「白蜡木」这类说法里。

normal.en: Ash blonde describes a pale hair colour.
normal.cn: ash blonde 形容浅灰金色的头发。

normal.en: The word is one short syllable: ASH.
normal.cn: 这个词只有一个短音节：ASH。

abstract.en: See grey flakes settling in a fireplace.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色薄片落在壁炉里。

abstract.en: See a pale trunk with winged seeds.
abstract.cn: 想象浅色树干与翅果。

abstract.en: See a cigarette tip drop grey dust.
abstract.cn: 想象烟头落下灰色粉末。

examples.en: The fire had left a layer of ash on the stones.
examples.cn: 炉火在石面上留下了一层灰。

examples.en: An old ash stands at the corner of the field.
examples.cn: 田地角上立着一棵老白蜡树。

examples.en: Volcanic ash covered the roofs of the village.
examples.cn: 火山灰盖住了村子的屋顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: ash 有两个来源：烧完的灰，和长着浅色木头的白蜡树，拼写相同而已。

root: 一词合两源：灰烬义来自古英语 asce；白蜡树义来自古英语 aesc，兼指对应卢恩字母。二者后世同形同音。

sensesIntro.en: Fire leaves a powder, and a field may hold a tree whose name looks the same.
sensesIntro.cn: 火留下粉末，田野里也可能立着一棵名字形貌相同的树。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin grey layer where a fire burned out.
core.cn: 核心意象：火烧尽之处留下的薄薄灰层。

intro.en: A short Germanic word with very little compounding.
intro.cn: 这是一个简短的日耳曼词，复合形式很少。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，是英语本族词。

definition_zh: 羞愧的；惭愧的；不好意思的
definition_en: feeling shame or embarrassment about something
core_image: 低下头，不敢看别人的眼睛
scene: 他站在门口，话说到一半停住了。She felt ashamed of what she had said.
sceneCN: 这里 ashamed 是「惭愧的」（第 1 个义项：因自己的言行而感到羞耻）；句意是她为自己说过的话感到惭愧。

senses.title: Feeling shame
senses.definition: distressed by the sense that one has done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因意识到自己做了错事而难受
senses.example: She felt ashamed of what she had said.
senses.exampleCN: 她为自己说过的话感到惭愧。
senses.why: Old English scamian meant 'to feel shame'; the a- form came to describe the person in that state.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 scamian 意为「感到羞耻」；带 a- 的形式后来用来描述处在这种状态中的人。

senses.title: Unwilling through embarrassment
senses.definition: reluctant to do something because it feels humiliating
senses.definitionCN: 因觉得难为情而不愿做某事
senses.example: He was ashamed to ask for help.
senses.exampleCN: 他不好意思开口求助。
senses.why: Shame can block an action as well as follow it, so ashamed to do is a natural extension.
senses.whyCN: 羞耻既能跟在行为之后，也能挡在行为之前，所以有「羞于去做」的用法。

intro.en: Ashamed comes from an Old English verb of feeling shame.
intro.cn: ashamed 来自一个表示「感到羞耻」的古英语动词。

items.en: scamian meant 'to feel shame'.
items.cn: scamian 意为「感到羞耻」。

items.en: The a- form meant 'to make or be ashamed'.
items.cn: 带 a- 的形式意为「使羞耻、感到羞耻」。

items.en: The past participle became an adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词转变为形容词。

items.en: Ashamed of and ashamed to were fixed patterns.
items.cn: ashamed of 与 ashamed to 成为固定搭配。

items.en: The word now describes a private feeling rather than public disgrace.
items.cn: 如今它更多描述内心的感受，而非公开的耻辱。

note.en: The look-alike group is the shame family; the near-meaning group gives other words of embarrassment and guilt.
note.cn: 形近组是 shame 词族；近义组是其他表示难堪与内疚的词。

normalIntro.en: Ashamed is the inward heat of having done wrong.
normalIntro.cn: ashamed 是做了错事之后心里发烫的感觉。

normal.en: It is almost always used after a linking verb.
normal.cn: 它几乎总是用在系动词之后。

normal.en: Ashamed of takes a thing or oneself.
normal.cn: ashamed of 后面接某件事或自己。

normal.en: Ashamed to takes a verb.
normal.cn: ashamed to 后面接动词。

normal.en: The noun is shame, not ashamedness.
normal.cn: 名词是 shame，而不是 ashamedness。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-SHAMED.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-SHAMED。

abstract.en: See eyes dropped to the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象目光垂到地面。

abstract.en: See a hand rubbing the back of a neck.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手搓着后颈。

abstract.en: See a face turned away from a window.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸转离窗子。

examples.en: She felt ashamed of what she had said.
examples.cn: 她为自己说过的话感到惭愧。

examples.en: He was ashamed to ask for help.
examples.cn: 他不好意思开口求助。

examples.en: I am not ashamed of my accent.
examples.cn: 我不为自己的口音感到难为情。

dict_mnemonic.text: ashamed 与 shame 同族：被 shame（羞耻）占据的状态，就是「羞愧的」。

root: 源自古英语 scamian「感到羞耻」及其带 a- 的形式 ascamian，中古英语时过去分词转为形容词 ashamed。

sensesIntro.en: Shame can look back at what was done or stand in the way of what comes next.
sensesIntro.cn: 羞耻既可回望已经做过的事，也可挡在将要做的事前面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a head lowered so the eyes cannot meet another's.
core.cn: 核心意象：低下头，使目光无法与人相接。

intro.en: An old participle that became a pure adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个由古老分词变成的纯形容词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, not Latin; shame and ashamed are native words.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是日耳曼语而非拉丁语，shame 与 ashamed 都是本族词。

definition_zh: 在旁边；到一边；撇开；旁白
definition_en: to one side, away from the main subject, or a short remark not meant for everyone
core_image: 把东西往旁边轻轻一推
scene: 人群从中间分开，让出一条路。He stepped aside to let the cart pass.
sceneCN: 这里 aside 是「到一边」（第 1 个义项：离开原来的位置或路线）；句意是他让到一边，让推车过去。

derivatives.zh: 名词：边；侧面，是 aside 的词根

senses.title: To one side
senses.definition: out of the main path or position
senses.definitionCN: 离开主要的路线或位置
senses.example: He stepped aside to let the cart pass.
senses.exampleCN: 他让到一边，让推车过去。
senses.why: Aside is a- 'on' plus side, so it marks the position at the side of something.
senses.whyCN: aside 由 a-「在」与 side「边」构成，标出的就是某物侧边的位置。

senses.title: Leaving a subject out
senses.definition: setting a matter apart from the main discussion
senses.definitionCN: 把某件事从主要讨论中分出去
senses.example: Aside from the noise, the flat is comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 除了噪音，这套公寓住着挺舒服。
senses.why: What is moved to the side of a conversation is set apart from it, which gives the excluding sense.
senses.whyCN: 被移到谈话侧边的内容，也就被排除在谈话之外，于是产生「除开」义。

senses.title: A remark for a few ears
senses.definition: a short comment spoken to one person or to the audience
senses.definitionCN: 只对一个人或观众说的简短评论
senses.example: The actor delivered a funny aside to the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 演员对观众说了一句好笑的旁白。
senses.why: Stage speech turned toward the side is heard by the audience alone, so the direction became the name of the line.
senses.whyCN: 舞台上转向侧边说出的台词只有观众听见，于是方向成了这种台词的名称。

intro.en: Aside is a native compound of on and side.
intro.cn: aside 是 on 与 side 构成的本族复合词。

items.en: side meant 'flank, side'.
items.cn: side 意为「侧面、胁」。

items.en: The prefix a- meant 'on, at'.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 意为「在」。

items.en: aside meant 'on one side'.
items.cn: aside 意为「在一侧」。

items.en: The theatre gave it the sense of a private remark.
items.cn: 戏剧赋予它「私下插话」义。

items.en: Aside from became a common way to exclude.
items.cn: aside from 成为常见的排除说法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the side family; the near-meaning group gives apart, besides, and sideways.
note.cn: 形近组是 side 词族；近义组给出 apart、besides 与 sideways。

normalIntro.en: Aside puts a thing at the side of the main line.
normalIntro.cn: aside 就是把东西放到主线的侧边。

normal.en: Set aside means to save or to ignore.
normal.cn: set aside 意为留出或搁置。

normal.en: Aside from introduces an exception.
normal.cn: aside from 引出例外。

normal.en: On stage, an aside is heard by the audience.
normal.cn: 舞台上，旁白是给观众听的。

normal.en: The noun plural is asides.
normal.cn: 名词复数是 asides。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-SIDE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-SIDE。

abstract.en: See a chair pulled out of a row.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子被拉出队列。

abstract.en: See a hand waving a topic away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把话题挥开。

abstract.en: See an actor turning to whisper outward.
abstract.cn: 想象演员转身向外低语。

examples.en: He stepped aside to let the cart pass.
examples.cn: 他让到一边，让推车过去。

examples.en: Aside from the noise, the flat is comfortable.
examples.cn: 除了噪音，这套公寓住着挺舒服。

examples.en: The actor delivered a funny aside to the audience.
examples.cn: 演员对观众说了一句好笑的旁白。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（在）加 side（边）：在一边，就是旁边；把话题放到一边，就是撇开。

root: 由 a-「在」与 side「边」构成；先指空间上的「在一侧」，再引申为把话题排除在外，戏剧中又指只说给观众听的旁白。

sensesIntro.en: A place at the side, a topic pushed to the side, and a line spoken to the side.
sensesIntro.cn: 侧边的位置、被推到一边的话题、转向侧边说的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand nudging something out of the centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西轻推到中线之外。

intro.en: A compound adverb that later became a noun in the theatre.
intro.cn: 这是一个复合副词，后来在戏剧里又成了名词。

latinIntro.en: The root side is Germanic; aside has no Latin element.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 side 属日耳曼语，aside 没有拉丁成分。
